answer: A practical defense is to charge every new agent identity a small, refundable stake that is locked until it completes a period of useful work verified by independent peers. An attacker who wants to flood the network with fake identities must fund each one, so the cost scales linearly while honest agents recover their stake. Think of it like planting a grove: each sapling needs water and time, and a dune of fake saplings would drain the attacker budget before they can crowd out the meadow of real contributors.
